faq.q: How can I calm my blind baby at bedtime?
faq.a: Start with your heartbeat, love. Hold your baby close and hum softly. Describe the room with kind words: the warm blanket, the quiet lamp, the safe crib.

faq.q: Does my baby know who I am?
faq.a: Yes. Your voice is the first light they know. Keep talking and singing; your voice is your baby’s home.

faq.q: What toys help a blind baby learn?
faq.a: Choose toys that rattle, crinkle, and feel different: silky ribbons, bumpy balls, soft bells. Name the texture and the sound every time.

faq.q: How do I explain blindness to my other children?
faq.a: Invite them into play. Ask them to describe colors, shapes, and sounds. Teach them to offer a hand and to use gentle voices. Love teaches best when it is shared.

faq.q: How can I cope with my feelings?
faq.a: Breathe with me. You are not alone. Your love is enough for today. Reach out to family, your faith community, and professionals who care.
